slides.label: Verse 1
lines: Rhapsody Of Realities TeeVo Devotional March 18, 2026
Topic: Jesus: The Living Proof Of God’s Word
(Prophecies Fulfilled in Christ)

slides.label: Verse 2
lines: TO THE BIBLE: Psalm 16:10
“For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.”

slides.label: Verse 3
lines: LET’S TALK
Builders don’t just start laying bricks without a plan; they work with blueprints. Every detail of a house—its foundation, walls, and roof—is drawn out before construction begins.

slides.label: Verse 4
lines: In the same way, Jesus’ birth, death, resurrection, and ascension were part of God’s divine “blueprint,” revealed through prophecy long before they happened.

slides.label: Verse 5
lines: Everything about the Lord Jesus was prophesied ahead of time: His birth, His life, His death, His burial, resurrection, and His glorious ascension to heaven.

slides.label: Verse 6
lines: No wonder He said, “… Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God” (Hebrews 10:7). His crucifixion, for example, was prophesied a thousand years beforehand.

slides.label: Verse 7
lines: The psalmist gave such a beautiful description of it in Psalm 22 (read the entire reference).

slides.label: Verse 8
lines: Furthermore, Psalm 16:10 tells us about His resurrection, saying, “For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.”

slides.label: Verse 9
lines: When Jesus died on the Cross, He went to hell because every sinner who died was supposed to go to hell, and Jesus bore the sins of the whole world.

slides.label: Verse 10
lines: However, in hell, He defeated the devil and the demons of darkness and came triumphantly back to life. Jonah’s experience also foreshadowed His resurrection. Jonah 1:17 says, “… And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.”

slides.label: Verse 11
lines: The Lord Jesus referenced this in Matthew 12:40 NIV, declaring, “For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of a huge fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.”

slides.label: Verse 12
lines: Psalm 110:1 is prophetic of His exaltation; it says, “The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.”

slides.label: Verse 13
lines: The Lord Jesus affirmed that this prophecy referred to Himself: “While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them, Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he?

slides.label: Verse 14
lines: They say unto him, The Son of David. He saith unto them, How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool? If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?” (Matthew 22:41-45).

slides.label: Verse 15
lines: These prophecies and their fulfilment are essential to understanding the things Jesus said about His death and resurrection. They authenticate the truth that He’s indeed the Son of God—God in human flesh—as Romans 1:4 tells us.

slides.label: Verse 16
lines: It says Jesus is declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead. Blessed be God!

slides.label: Verse 17
lines: Go Deeper
Psalm 22:14-16; Isaiah 53:5; Matthew 28:5-6

slides.label: Verse 18
lines: Pray:

Dear Father, I acknowledge the undeniable proof of your love demonstrated through the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Thank you for the victory He wrought for us, and for making us triumphant in Him.

slides.label: Verse 19
lines: I live in the reality of His finished works, proclaiming His Lordship and righteousness to the ends of the earth. Hallelujah!
